SCR POWER CONTROL CIRCUIT
This is a typical SCR power control circuit................
DISCUSSION
The purpose of this circuit is to rectify and control the amount of power applied to the load.
The SCR Power Control Circuit has an input circuit to apply gate current (Ig) to turn ON the SCR. A separate voltage source maybe used.
R1 is used for cathode bias. C1 and C2 are DC blocking capacitors.
Note that it does not have a reset circuit.
Since an AC signal is applied, once the SCR is reverse biased, Ia (Anode current) stops. This action turns OFF the SCR.
Only when the SCR is forward biased will the action of the gate turn ON the SCR.
In this power control circuit, which component comprises the input circuit?
R1 is connected to the cathode of SCR1. It is not in the gate (or input) circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
C1 is connected to the cathode of SCR1. It is not in the gate (or input) circuit.
TRY AGAIN!
In this power control circuit, which component comprises the reset circuit?
The SCR power control circuit is an AC circuit. When the SCR is reverse biased, it resets automatically.
TRY AGAIN!
The operation of a power control circuit is based on controlling the amount of TIME that AC voltage is sent to the load.
If the full 360 degrees of the AC input voltage is applied to the load, a certain maximum amount of power is used.
However, the SCR is a diode. This reduces the amount of AC applied to the load by half (180 degrees). The power is 50% of maximum.
In addition, the gate on the SCR controls when the SCR turns ON during the time that the SCR is forward biased.
If the gate voltage turns ON the SCR only for half of the forward biased alternation, the power is reduced to 25% of maximum.
By controlling the gate voltage (gate current), the time that the load receives voltage is controlled, which controls the amount of power.
How is power to a load controlled in a SCR power controlled circuit?
The amount of time that voltage is applied to the load.
The SCR does rectify the AC input voltage. However, this places the power used at 50% of maximum with no control.
TRY AGAIN!
The amplitude of the input signal determines the maximum amount of power that could be used. It does not control the power used.
TRY AGAIN!
Now, let's take a look at the waveforms in a SCR power control circuit.
At 0 degrees of the input signal, the signals across the load resistor and SCR are as shown.
From 0 to 90 degrees of the input signal, the SCR is forward biased. Assume that the SCR has not turned ON so current does not flow through the load.
At 90 degrees assume the action of R1, R2 and C2 develop enough voltage that produces an Ig large enough to turn ON the SCR.
The time between 0 and 90 degrees is called the FIRE ANGLE. In this case the fire angle is 90 degrees.
During the time from 90 degrees to 180 degrees, the SCR is conducting. The SCR is a short circuit.
The time between 90 and 180 degrees is called the CONDUCTION ANGLE. In this case the conduction angle is also 90 degrees..es.
The sum of the fire angle and conduction is always equal to180 degrees.
During the time from 180 to 360 degrees the SCR is reverse biased and current does not flow. The SCR is reset automatically.
Note the voltage is developed across the load for only 90 degrees of the input signal. Remember, Power equals the voltage squared divided by the resistance.O
If R2 is changed so that the gate current will not turn ON the SCR until after 90 degrees, the power to the load is less.
Note that if the fire angle is 135degrees, the conduction angle is 45 degrees.
If R2 is changed so that the gate current will turn ON the SCR between 0 and 90 degrees, the power to the load is greater.
Note that if the fire angle is 45 degrees, the conduction angle is 135 degrees.
By varying R2, the fire angle is changed between 0 and 180 degrees which controls the amount of power to the load.

The SCR's ultimate effect is controlling the time that the average voltage of the source is applied to the load.
The approximate average voltage is calculated by multiplying the RMS value of the input sine wave by the number of degrees of the sine wave that the SCR controls, divided by 360. 60.
For example, if an SCR conducts (conduction angle) for 120 degrees of a 60 Hz, 120 V peak sine wave, the average voltage applied to the load is 28 VDC.

1. The purpose of a SCR power control circuit is to rectify and control the amount of power applied to the load.
2. The voltage applied to the gate turns ON the SCR for a portion of the forward bias alternation of the input waveform. During the reverse biased alternation the SCR is turned OFF..
3. The amount of time that the SCR is ON determines the amount of voltage, and consequently the amount of power, to the load.
4. The number of degrees before the SCR turns ON is the firing angle. The number of degrees after the SCR turns ON is the conduction angle. Their total is always 180 degrees..
5. The average voltage applied to the load equals the RMS value of the input sine wave times the conduction angle divided by 360 degrees.
